trust_boundaries.name: TB-1 Prysm keystore key derivation (loader.rs:load_from_prysm_format)
trust_boundaries.assumption: PBKDF2-derived 32-byte key; only lower 16 bytes used for AES-128-CTR. Key is attacker-influenced via password file.
trust_boundaries.evidence: decryption_key[..16] used for key, decryption_key[16..] silently discarded — only 128 bits of entropy consumed from a 256-bit derivation.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-2 ERC2335 proxy delegation load (store.rs:load_proxies)
trust_boundaries.assumption: Delegation signature loaded from .sig file on disk, deserialized as BlsSignature — NOT re-validated against the delegator public key during load.
trust_boundaries.evidence: trust_level: unverified used as validated. If .sig file is tampered, the proxy signer operates with an invalid delegation.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-3 JWT decode/validate coupling (utils.rs:decode_jwt / validate_jwt)
trust_boundaries.assumption: decode_jwt extracts module_id with signature validation explicitly disabled; validate_jwt then checks the signature. Race or call-order confusion could allow using a decoded-but-unvalidated module_id.
trust_boundaries.evidence: Separation of decode and validate is a design-level coupling risk; callers must always call both in correct order.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-4 Secret key bytes lifetime (schemes/bls.rs, schemes/ecdsa.rs)
trust_boundaries.assumption: Raw secret key bytes returned as Vec<u8> / [u8;32] with no zeroize-on-drop, used in ProxyStore::store_proxy_bls/ecdsa for serialization to disk.
trust_boundaries.evidence: Key material persists in heap memory after use.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-5 GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT domain (signature.rs:compute_domain)
trust_boundaries.assumption: GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT is hardcoded to [0;32]; intentional for builder domains but must also be correct for COMMIT_BOOST_DOMAIN usage.
trust_boundaries.evidence: Domain computed with zero GVR — cross-chain replay possible if domain separation relies solely on fork version.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-6 Module authorization scope (service.rs:handle_request_signature)
trust_boundaries.assumption: No per-module restriction on which consensus pubkeys a module can request signatures for. Any module with a valid JWT can sign with any consensus key.
trust_boundaries.evidence: module_id is verified but not checked against the requested pubkey's allowed signers.

trust_boundaries.name: TB-7 Plaintext proxy store (store.rs:ProxyStore::File)
trust_boundaries.assumption: Plaintext proxy store writes raw secret bytes to disk as JSON. Marked 'do not use in prod' but present in codebase.
trust_boundaries.evidence: Production guard is documentation only, not enforced in code.

critical_paths.name: BLS signing pipeline (consensus)
critical_paths.entry: handle_request_signature -> LocalSigningManager::sign_consensus -> ConsensusSigner::sign -> sign_commit_boost_root -> compute_domain + compute_signing_root -> BlsSecretKey::sign
critical_paths.risk: HIGH — domain construction and signing root are the last line of defense against cross-protocol replay

critical_paths.name: Proxy delegation creation and validation
critical_paths.risk: HIGH — delegation binds proxy key to consensus key; if domain or message encoding is wrong, delegations are forgeable

critical_paths.name: ERC-2335 proxy key load path
critical_paths.entry: ProxyStore::load_proxies (ERC2335) -> load_bls_signer / load_ecdsa_signer -> BlsProxySigner construction WITHOUT re-validating delegation signature

critical_paths.name: Prysm keystore decryption
critical_paths.entry: load_from_prysm_format -> pbkdf2 -> AES-128-CTR (lower 16 bytes of 32-byte key) -> JSON parse -> ConsensusSigner
critical_paths.risk: MEDIUM — key derivation and IV handling need review; only 128 bits used from 256-bit PBKDF2 output

critical_paths.name: JWT authentication flow
critical_paths.entry: jwt_auth middleware -> decode_jwt (no sig check) -> validate_jwt (sig check) -> module_id inserted into request extensions
critical_paths.risk: MEDIUM — two-step auth with insecure decode-first is fragile; must verify no code path uses module_id between decode and validate

critical_paths.name: ECDSA proxy signing
critical_paths.risk: MEDIUM — secp256k1 signing with COMMIT_BOOST_DOMAIN; verify EIP-712 / replay protection

unresolved_assumptions: DIM-2: Confirm the AES-128-CTR 32->16 byte key truncation matches the Prysm spec and is not a truncation bug (resolved FALSE POSITIVE in NF-02).

route_dispositions.summary: BLS/ECDSA signing pipeline, domain construction, and delegation binding reviewed; F-01..F-04 raised.
Prysm keystore AES-128-CTR path lacks MAC/checksum verification (F-05) and has an unbounded PBKDF2 iteration parameter (F-06).
Secret bytes not zeroized after use (F-04); zero-address guard missing in verify_ecdsa_signature (F-07).
blstrs_plus is an untagged internal fork of blstrs (DEP-01); no exploitable bug in current usage.
JWT two-step auth (NF-01) and Prysm AES key truncation (NF-02) dismissed as false positives after verification.

verified_findings.summary: ERC-2335 proxy delegation not re-validated on load. BlsProxySigner is constructed with a delegation loaded from .sig file without calling validate(); a tampered .sig file installs an invalid delegation silently. (crates/common/src/signer/store.rs:354-369)

Any authenticated module can request consensus key signatures. handle_request_signature dispatches SignRequest::Consensus without checking that the requesting module_id is authorized for the requested pubkey. (crates/signer/src/service.rs:278-281)

GVR=0 enables cross-chain replay for custom chain deployments. Named chains safe (distinct fork_versions); two Chain::Custom deployments sharing the same fork_version produce identical COMMIT_BOOST_DOMAINs. (crates/common/src/constants.rs:2, signature.rs:40)

BLS and ECDSA secret bytes not zeroized after use. secret() returns raw key bytes with no ZeroizeOnDrop; Bytes/Vec locals in store.rs not zeroized after serialization. (schemes/bls.rs:31-35, schemes/ecdsa.rs:80-83, store.rs:88,103,125,140)

Prysm keystore decryption lacks MAC/checksum verification. PrysmKeystore omits crypto.checksum; AES-128-CTR decryption proceeds without any integrity check, allowing attacker-crafted ciphertext to substitute arbitrary BLS keys. (loader.rs:232-279, types.rs:46-125)

Prysm PBKDF2 iteration count attacker-controllable, no minimum enforced. keystore.c read from attacker-controllable JSON with no bounds check; c=1 degrades the KDF, c=u32::MAX causes DoS hang. (loader.rs:254-257)
verify_ecdsa_signature does not reject zero address (latent). No check that recovered != Address::ZERO; currently only used in tests, latent risk for future callers. (schemes/ecdsa.rs:109-117)
blstrs_plus is an untagged internal fork of blstrs (Cargo.toml:90 commit c4ea6b21). Divergence from upstream blstrs 0.7.1 unaudited; no exploitable bug found in current usage.

fp_check_verdicts.rationale: check_jwt_auth correctly sequences decode->lookup->validate; module_id not used for any security decision before validation. (service.rs:206-228)
AES-128-CTR uses first 16 bytes of 32-byte PBKDF2 output, correct per EIP-2335 for AES-128. (loader.rs:261)

dimension_map_anomalies.description: BlsSignature loaded from .sig file has trust_level=unverified but is used as validated. No call to SignedProxyDelegation::validate() in ERC2335 load path.
PBKDF2 produces 32 bytes; only decryption_key[..16] fed to AES-128-CTR. Correct (AES-128 takes 16-byte key) but discards the upper half silently — worth confirming this matches the Prysm spec.

GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT = [0;32]. compute_domain uses this for all domains. Any chain where GVR differs means COMMIT_BOOST_DOMAIN is the same across all chains that share a fork_version, enabling cross-chain replay of signed proxy delegations.
SignRequest::Consensus carries only a pubkey + object_root. The signer service verifies the JWT module_id but does not check that module_id is authorized to sign with that consensus pubkey.
BlsSigner::secret() returns [u8;32] and EcdsaSigner::secret() returns Vec<u8>. Neither type implements zeroize::Zeroize or Drop with zeroize. Key bytes may linger in heap/stack after use.

threat_model_notes: Replay prevention: SignedProxyDelegation binds delegator+proxy pubkeys and uses COMMIT_BOOST_DOMAIN. However GVR=0 means the domain is identical across all Ethereum networks sharing the same fork_version byte, enabling cross-network replay of signed delegations.

Key authentication chain: consensus_signers map is populated from SignerLoader (file / validators_dir). No chain-of-trust verification at signer service startup — keys are trusted once loaded. Delegation signatures are verified at creation but NOT at load time for ERC2335.
CSPRNG: BlsSigner::new_random() -> BlsSecretKey::random(); EcdsaSigner::new_random() -> PrivateKeySigner::random(). Both use OS-backed RNG via rand 0.9 with os_rng feature. Acceptable.
Downgrade resistance: No protocol version negotiation in the signing API. Not applicable here.
Authorization scope: JWT identifies the module but does not restrict which keys the module can use — all consensus keys are available to any authenticated module.
